newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH says div change to benefit offshore s/holders.
newsitem.headline: CHH says div change to benefit offshore s/holders.

text.p: Carter Holt Harvey Ltd on Thursday declared an interim dividend of five NZ cents per share with full tax credits.

The company said changes to the method of crediting the dividend would benefit New Zealand resident shareholders paying tax at less than the top rate of 33 percent, and non-New Zealand resident shareholders.
"The company has determined that it will credit this dividend with dividend withholding payments (DWP) credits rather than imputation credits. No shareholder will be disadvantaged by this," CHH said.
For most New Zealand resident shareholders, the position would be the same as if they had received a fully imputed dividend.
New Zealand resident shareholders who pay tax at less than 33 percent will be entitled to a cash refund for the excess of the DWP credits over their tax liability.
For non-New Zealand shareholders the DWP credits are first applied to meet the shareholders' non-resident withholding tax liability and the excess is refundable in cash.
This refund will be paid to them with their dividend and it represents an increase in the effective dividend of 27 percent.

This means that non-resident shareholders will receive NZ 1.34328 cents in addition to the dividend of five cents. This is the refund of the DWP credits attached in excess of the non-resident withholding tax, CHH said. The five cent dividend is unchanged from last year's interim payout.
Carter Holt is just over half owned by International Paper.
